proposals.before: Yuanjing was killed by Jinghe; Shilong, because he was far away, escaped.
proposals.after: Yuanjing was killed in the Jinghe era; Shilong, because he was far away, escaped.
proposals.reason: Jinghe (景和) is a reign-period name, not a person who killed Yuanjing; the literal English wrongly treats it as an agent.

proposals.before: He spoke of him to Emperor Xiaowu, and Shilong was summoned to audience. The emperor said: 「Of the Three Dukes there will be one—and that will be a matter for the future.」
proposals.after: He spoke of him to Emperor Xiaowu, and Shilong was summoned to audience. The emperor said: "One of the Three Dukes—that will be a matter for the future."
proposals.reason: The bracketed literal obscures the emperor's prediction that Shilong would become one of the Three Dukes; align with the clear idiomatic sense while staying close to 三公一人，是將來事也.

proposals.before: Their outer rampart is not strategically vital; clear it, and leave thirty paces from the inner wall—that is best.
proposals.after: Their outer rampart is not strategically vital; clear it, and leave thirty zhang from the inner metal wall—that is best.
proposals.reason: Chinese 三十丈 is the length measure zhang, not paces; the idiomatic translation misrenders the unit and drops 金城 as metal/inner wall.

proposals.before: Ying had not yet sent pursuers, but the scattered soldiers feared Miao raids and gathered again—about twenty thousand—following Youzhi; when they were nearing Jiangling they then dispersed.
proposals.after: Ying had not yet sent pursuers, but the scattered soldiers feared Man/tribal raids and gathered again—about twenty thousand—following Youzhi; when they were nearing Jiangling they then dispersed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 蠻 is Man/tribal peoples in general; literal English wrongly specifies Miao.

proposals.before: Illness made him yield his post; he was offered Palace Attendant and Guardian General, declined, and was made Grand Master of the Palace Encampment instead, with Palace Attendant unchanged.
proposals.after: Illness made him yield his post; he was offered Palace Attendant and Guardian General, declined, and was made Left Household Grandee instead, with Palace Attendant unchanged.
proposals.reason: 左光祿大夫 is Left Household Grandee, not Grand Master of the Palace Encampment; the same title is rendered Household Grandee in s0153.

proposals.before: Illness made him yield his post; he was reassigned Palace Attendant and Guardian General; he did not accept, and was moved to Grand Master of the Palace Encampment, retaining Palace Attendant as before.
proposals.after: Illness made him yield his post; he was reassigned Palace Attendant and Guardian General; he did not accept, and was moved to Left Household Grandee, retaining Palace Attendant as before.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise mistranslates 左光祿大夫 as Grand Master of the Palace Encampment.

proposals.before: Another edict read: "The late Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, bore virtue in his work and joined talent to the warp and woof of rule.
proposals.after: Another edict read: "The late Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, bore virtue in his work and joined talent to the warp and woof of rule.
proposals.reason: 侍中 was already rendered Palace Attendant in this chapter; Attendant-in-Ordinary is the usual rendering of 散騎常侍, not 侍中.

proposals.before: Shilong was versed in number-craft; at Nitang he laid out a tomb and walked the ground with guests—nine visits in ten he would sit in the same place.
proposals.after: Shilong was versed in number-craft; at Nitang he laid out a tomb and walked the ground with guests—going ten times and five, he would always sit in the same place.
proposals.reason: 十往五往 means repeated comings and goings, not a nine-out-of-ten frequency.

proposals.before: Shilong was skilled in divination; at Nitang he opened a tomb and walked the site with guests—nine times in ten he would sit in the same spot.
proposals.after: Shilong was skilled in divination; at Nitang he opened a tomb and walked the site with guests—ten goings and five goings, he would always sit in the same spot.
proposals.reason: Literal English invents a nine-in-ten ratio not present in 十往五往.

proposals.before: Gui left office as acting staff under the Grand Marshal of Prince Jiangxia, was assigned to outer military affairs, and with the headquarters became a Five Offices aide under the Grand Tutor—favored by Yigong.
proposals.after: Gui doffed plain clothes as acting staff under the Grand Marshal of Prince Jiangxia, was assigned to outer military affairs, and with the headquarters became a Five Offices aide under the Grand Tutor—favored by Yigong.
proposals.reason: 解褐 means beginning official service by putting off coarse clothing, not leaving office.

proposals.before: He rose to Crown Prince Attendant, Secretariat Director, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
proposals.after: He rose to Crown Prince Attendant, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant Gentleman of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
proposals.reason: 中書郎 is Secretariat Gentleman, not Director; 司徒 is Minister of Education, not Minister of Works (司空).

proposals.before: He was promoted to Crown Prince Attendant, Secretariat Director, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
proposals.after: He was promoted to Crown Prince Attendant, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant Gentleman of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslations as in the idiomatic field: 中書郎 and 司徒.

proposals.before: Another edict said: 「The late Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, upheld virtue in his station and united talent with statecraft.
proposals.after: Another edict said: 「The late Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, upheld virtue in his station and united talent with statecraft.
proposals.reason: 侍中 should be Palace Attendant, consistent with earlier units; Attendant-in-Ordinary mistranslates the office.

proposals.before: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Palace Attendant as before.
proposals.reason: 侍中如故 continues Palace Attendant, not Attendant-in-Ordinary.

proposals.before: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Palace Attendant as before.
proposals.reason: 侍中如故 is Palace Attendant as before.

proposals.before: He was named General Who Exerts Might and Administrator of Donghai and Dongguan, but declined.
proposals.after: He was named Champion General and Administrator of Donghai and Dongguan, but declined.
proposals.reason: 冠軍將軍 is Champion General, not General Who Exerts Might (a rendering that fits 奮武 or similar, not 冠軍).

proposals.before: He was appointed General Who Exerts Might and Administrator of the two commanderies Donghai and Dongguan, but did not accept,
proposals.after: He was appointed Champion General and Administrator of the two commanderies Donghai and Dongguan, but did not accept,
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 冠軍將軍 as General Who Exerts Might in the literal field.

proposals.before: In the second year he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat while keeping his commandant post.
proposals.after: In the second year he became Director of Capital Officials while keeping his commandant post.
proposals.reason: 都官尚書 is the Director of the Capital Officials / justice section, not the Imperial Secretariat as a whole.

proposals.before: In the second year he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat while keeping his commandant post.
proposals.after: In the second year he became Director of Capital Officials while keeping his commandant post.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation of 都官尚書 in the literal field.

proposals.before: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he was General Who Exerts Might, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang's Northern Army, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; when the headquarters moved he became chief aide of the expeditionary force.
proposals.after: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he was Champion General, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang as Northern Palace Cadet, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; when the headquarters moved he became chief aide of the expeditionary force.
proposals.reason: 冠軍將軍 again mistranslated; 北中郎長史 is chief aide to the Northern Palace Cadet (General), not 'Northern Army'.

proposals.before: Once he took office he pleaded illness again and came back as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendor.
proposals.after: Once he took office he pleaded illness again and came back as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
proposals.reason: Chinese 散騎常侍、光祿大夫 matches s0201; 'Outer Attendant' and inconsistent office/title English are invented variants.

proposals.before: On reaching his post he again pleaded illness and returned to serve as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendor.
proposals.after: On reaching his post he again pleaded illness and returned to serve as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
proposals.reason: Same inconsistent rendering of 散騎常侍、光祿大夫 versus s0201.

proposals.before: In year 3 the righteous army came south; Dong Hun lent Gui his staff and set him to hold Shitou.
proposals.after: In year 3 the righteous army came south; the Marquis of Donghun lent Gui his staff and set him to hold Shitou.
proposals.reason: 東昏 is the epithet/title of the deposed emperor (東昏侯), not a personal name 'Dong Hun'.

proposals.before: When the Shizu Emperor acceded, he was General Who Exerts Might, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang's Northern Army, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; he shifted with the headquarters to chief aide of the expeditionary force.
proposals.after: When the Shizu Emperor acceded, he was Champion General, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang as Northern Palace Cadet, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; he shifted with the headquarters to chief aide of the expeditionary force.
proposals.reason: 冠軍將軍 is Champion General; 北中郎長史 is chief aide to the Northern Palace Cadet, not 'Northern Army'.

proposals.before: He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army, then was promoted to General Who Exerts Might and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
proposals.after: He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army, then was promoted to Champion General and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
proposals.reason: 冠軍將軍 is Champion General, not General Who Exerts Might.

proposals.before: He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army; he was promoted to General Who Exerts Might and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
proposals.after: He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army; he was promoted to Champion General and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 冠軍將軍 in the literal field.

decisions.reason: s0011 元景爲景和所殺 uses the reign title 景和 as the era of the killing, not a personal agent; “killed by Jinghe” invents a person, while “killed in the Jinghe era” matches the Chinese and the idiomatic purge sense.
s0007 三公一人，是將來事也 is already conveyed by the original literal’s prediction that one of the Three Dukes lies in the future; the proposed rewording is stylistic and does not correct a semantic error.
s0122 使去金城三十丈 has the length unit 丈 and the fortified 金城; “thirty paces” and bare “inner wall” misrender both terms, which the proposal restores.

decisions.after: Ying had not yet sent pursuers, but the scattered soldiers feared Man raids and gathered again—about twenty thousand—following Youzhi; when they were nearing Jiangling they then dispersed.
decisions.reason: s0097 畏蠻抄 refers to Man/southern tribal peoples generally, not the Miao; the proposal correctly drops Miao, but the slash form “Man/tribal” is awkward—plain “Man raids” fits the literal field.
s0150 轉左光祿大夫 is Left Household Grandee (光祿大夫); “Grand Master of the Palace Encampment” invents a different office the proposal correctly replaces.
The literal of s0150 likewise mistranslates 左光祿大夫; Left Household Grandee matches the title and the chapter’s later Household Grandee rendering.
s0153 故侍中 is Palace Attendant; Attendant-in-Ordinary is the standard English for 散騎常侍, not 侍中, so the proposal corrects a real office error.

decisions.after: Shilong was versed in number-craft; at Nitang he laid out a tomb and walked the ground with guests—whether ten visits or five, he always sat in the same place.
decisions.reason: s0166 十往五往 marks repeated visits, not a nine-in-ten ratio; the original invents that frequency, but “going ten times and five” is awkward—prefer “whether ten visits or five.”

decisions.after: Shilong was skilled in divination; at Nitang he opened a tomb and walked the site with guests—whether ten goings or five, he always sat in the same spot.
decisions.reason: The literal’s “nine times in ten” invents a ratio absent from 十往五往; the proposal’s “ten goings and five goings” is still clumsy—revise to “whether ten goings or five.”

decisions.after: Gui doffed plain clothes to serve as acting staff under the Grand Marshal of Prince Jiangxia, was assigned to outer military affairs, and with the headquarters became a Five Offices aide under the Grand Tutor—favored by Yigong.
decisions.reason: s0176 解褐 marks first entry into office by doffing coarse cloth, not leaving office; “doffed plain clothes as” is still awkward—insert “to serve as” for clear English.
